label: late original-phase input of o/q/e/l/g/v/3/b/m after y/digit/r/d/p/c/j-rich prefix
explanation: Fires almost only during the original (input) phase at orig_idx >= 3 (99.8% of mass; never at t<3, never in the copy phase, a trace on <DEL>). Fires when the input token is in a specific set: o and q most strongly (~5.7x lift), then e, l, g, then v, 3, b, m; other tokens almost never trigger it. Whether it fires on those tokens depends on the earlier prefix: the rate goes up when the earlier tokens include several of y, 0, 1, 2, r, d, p, c, j (first_tok y gives 3.2x, and the rate also climbs with digit count). It goes down when earlier inputs already came from the trigger set. First occurrences of a token account for 92% of mass. Rate climbs with position and peaks at orig_idx 5-8. The top activations are on o/q/e right before <DEL> in prefixes like "y d 0 ..." or "j 2 c r ...". The token-set-plus-position predicate alone covers 98% of mass at only 12% precision. Adding the prefix condition gives F1 ~0.38 and mass recall ~0.88 on dev. The context dependence is graded, so no crisp rule reaches high precision.
